recipes.name: Fish Chowder
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds cod, diced into 1/2 inch cubes
0.125 teaspoon Old Bay Seasoning TM, or to taste
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Melt butter in a large stockpot over medium heat. Sauté onions, mushrooms, and celery in butter until tender. Add chicken stock and potatoes; simmer for 10 minutes. Add fish; simmer for another 10 minutes.
Mix together clam juice and flour in a small bowl until smooth; stir into soup and simmer for 1 minute. Season with Old Bay, salt, and pepper. Remove from heat and stir in evaporated milk.
Portion into soup bowls and top with crumbled bacon.

raw_recipe.headline: Fish Chowder
raw_recipe.description: This fish chowder recipe makes a rich and comforting soup with fresh cod, clam juice, potatoes, and crispy bacon in a delicious creamy broth.

review.reviewBody:
“What’s Old Bay?” you ask. Try this: celery seed, black pepper, bay leaf, cardamom, mustard seed, cloves, paprika, and mace. 

Didn’t have cod, so I added shrimp during the last 5 minutes of cooking. (Don’t overcook shrimp, otherwise they get rubbery).Also didn’t have clam juice, so I used extra chicken stock. Instead of evaporated milk, I used 2%. As others mentioned, I added corn, extra mushrooms, and crumbled bacon on top.

Mmm...Mmm...Good!

This really was easy and extremely adaptable. I used catfish, but any white fish would work well - even a mixture of fish. I increased the Old Bay Seasoning to 1 tsp +, and added the entire bottle of clam juice. I also added 1 Tbls more than called for of flour, to make it a little thicker. Next time I'll add the crumbled bacon into the soup, rather than use as a topping. Top with parsley. KEEPER!

This recipe was thorough in timing if you follow the amounts given. I used fresh trout which was very good. Also used 1 teas fish sauce and a cup of water for clam juice. Can use creole seasoning for old bay if need be in a pinch. This was a favorite dish of my husbands. I left out the mushrooms didn't have any.

This makes a lot...if you halve the recipe you get six good servings. I found the taste improved by sauteing the vegetables in bacon drippings, increasing the Old Bay seasoning to about 1.5 tsp, adding 3/4 tsp. of salt when adding the potatoes, keeping the clam juice at 1 c when halving the recipe, and finishing with a tbsp. of butter when the evap. milk was added. Really excellent! Thank you, Amy!

I love this recipe. I have made this several times now- it was a huge hit for Christmas eve dinner. I add shrimp, scallops, clams and corn as well. Must be careful to not cook too much after adding cod(or haddock) because it breaks down, so I add it in big chunks & cook it for several minutes longer until cooked thru. I also add a splash of sherry and some extra butter- yum!! Thanks!

This really is a good fish chowder. My prep was just a bit different; I love to simmer broths! I had thick tilapia filets, so just sprinkled them with Old Bay and tossed that in the fridge till needed. I sauteed the veggies in bacon fat with added poblano because I had it. Added the potatoes, fish stock, half the clam juice, Old Bay and milk. Then simmered all that for like thirty minutes. I had fresh corn that I had grilled, so cut it from the cob and tossed that in to use it up too. Then added the chopped fish and thickened with the remaining clam juice and flour mixture. And then remembered I had cooked, peeled shrimp so added a few of those. Good, solid recipe that can be easily altered to personal tastes. Will be keeping this one because using the condensed milk made it so much more light on the stomach than heavy cream.

I used chunks of Sheephead from a 9 pounder I caught. Came out delicious. I seasoned the fish with a generous amount of old bay after cutting into cubes and let sit in fridge 1/2 hr. Started with homemade chicken broth. I also put a couple spoonfuls of the bacon grease I got from frying the fresh bacon for the topping. It really made the taste! Used half and half, extra salt and pepper and old bay, and some lawrys season salt. Really loved it so did the family, will definitely make again.

we loved it! thank you for the recipe. made it per the recipe just added a splash of white wine to the saute and a couple carrots for color. oh and just for our preference we like chowders spicier (added cayenne) and on the thick side so i added a few instant potato flakes at the end to quick thicken it which was great but i think it did change the texture from what was intended, we were hungry though no time to flour thicken again. flavor was wonderful and delicate, we topped with a few french fried onions and paired with an alton brown recipe for creamed corn corn bread with a drizzle of maple syrup. yum went nicely with the spicy chowder. one thing maybe someone can tell me, but my fish sort of disappeared texture wise. i followed the recipe and i didn't have any chunks of fish. it was still really great, maybe that's how it's suppose to be. maybe i needed thicker fillets.

Delicious recipe — loved the addition of the mushrooms. We used an 8 oz package of sliced baby Bella’s. I also used quite a bit more Old Bay. The major thing we did differently is I added about 4 cups of bite size cauliflower florets and added 2 more cups of broth so that everything would be covered. It was really delicious and the bacon sends it over the top.

This was good and a nice way to use up some fish and scallops I had in the freezer. I followed the recipe but instead of adding flour, I left my potatoes fairly large and mashed them a bit and then only used 1/2 of one can of evaporated milk. I did not have mushrooms so I simply left them out. I think they would have made this even better. I did use more Old Bay. I will made this again.

This recipe is delicious. I used half the potatoes, added 1/4 cup of grated carrots, added 1/4 cup of corn kernels, and increased the Old Bay seasoning to 1 teaspoon. I substituted 2 cups of half-and-half for the 2 cans of evaporated milk, 1 teaspoon of fish sauce for the clam juice, 4 oz canned mushrooms but the fresh, and 1/4 cup of corn starch for the flour to make it gluten free. Then I added 1 Tbsp dried parsley, 2 Tbsp brandy, 1 Tbsp Madeira wine, and 1/2 tsp of sherry vinegar to finish it. Wife went back for seconds. Good stuff!
Evaporated milk made it so oily you couldn’t taste anything no matter how many spices. $40 was wasted on my fish. Oh welll.
I am going to add this to my list of meals! Wonderful!

Love this recipe! Super tasty. Used crappie we caught here locally and added oysters, shrimp and clams but otherwise stuck to the script. Tasted as good as any chowder I've ordered at upscale restaurants. Definitely a keeper!

Loved it! I used perch & crappie fillets instead of cod & heavy cream instead of evaporated mllk. The heavy cream made it much richer and I found a new way to use the fish I catch! I also added some of my favorite creole seasoning for some added zest! It was excellent! As close to New England clam chowder as we get in northern MN!

I gave it four stars only because I tweaked it slightly. I used 1 Tablespoon of butter and 1 Tablespoon of Bacon Up (no bacon as it is for a Friday during Lent)for softening the vegetables. I used an ounce of dried oyster mushrooms that I rehydrated with a bottle of heated up clam juice. I added a splash of dry Vermouth (it is what I had in hand) to the recipe somewhere along the line. I used a teaspoon of Old Bay as per other reviews and I used light cream vs evaporated milk. It was very well received at the Lenten potluck!

I've made this chowder a few of times. Although It's absolutely delicious as-written, here are a few small tweaks I'd recommend. 1) Brown your bacon in your soup pot and leave about a tablespoon of the bacon fat behind in place of some of the butter, it adds a little more flavor to the onions and celery. 2) Don't be shy with the Old Bay and try a little fresh thyme to taste (it's a classic New England Chowder herb) . 3) If you don't have evaporated milk on hand, light cream works very well too. In fact, I prefer it.
very tasty

This is a great recipe. I used whiting fish, frozen, a 2lb package and chopped it up. I had some leftover heavy cream (about ¾ of a cup) so I used that and one can of evaporated milk. I added extra mushrooms and did 1 tsp of Old Bay as others recommended, and those were definitely good additions. Served with some good Italian bread, it was a fantastic winter dinner. You may want to cut the recipe in half unless you're cooking for a lot of people- this makes quite a lot of chowder.
Added extra mushrooms. Delicious.
